action: Completed all four sections of 90-day Economic Resilience Framework draft; held peer conversation with Lisa Freeman at community center; issued public statement naming specific resources and contacts; reached out to Millfield Community College about paid advisory/instructional role
narrative: Maria Santos finished the Economic Resilience Framework this tick — all four sections, including the small business stabilization fund utilization review (recommending the revenue decline threshold drop from 15% to 10% and eligibility expansion to sole proprietors) and the adaptive reuse zoning recommendation for the auto row corridor, which she is calling a 'Mobility and Logistics Transition Zone.' She met with Lisa Freeman at the community center for forty minutes and left with two specific fixes to make: routing the grant committee inquiry line to Nadia Osei's direct phone number on the municipal website, and adding a Spanish-language contact option. The public statement went out, naming Lisa Freeman and Nadia Osei directly. Separately, she emailed the workforce program director at Millfield Community College, Dr. Kevin Marsh, asking whether there is a paid advisory or instructional role available given her role as architect of the retraining fund — he replied the same day expressing real interest and scheduling a call for next week. Income is not resolved, but the first credible lead is in motion.
